title: House
subtitle: Jack first, footwork second. Everything else is decoration.
description: House dance is built from the chest down: a bounce that never stops, footwork that rides it, and travel that keeps you moving through the room. Work the stages in order — every later step assumes the pulse from stage one is still running underneath it.

stages.title: Find the pulse
stages.description: Before any footwork, get the bounce into your body. If the jack stops, the dance stops.

steps.title: The jack
steps.description: The core of house — a chest-to-pelvis wave that rocks you on the beat. Learn it standing still and keep it running under every step that follows.

steps.title: Bounce on one leg
steps.description: The same pulse with your weight parked on one side. This is what lets you free a foot without losing the groove.

steps.title: Knee up
steps.description: Alternating knee lifts on the beat. The first step where the jack and the legs have to agree with each other.

steps.title: Loose legs
steps.description: Let the knees swing in and out under a relaxed upper body. Not a step so much as a permission — house footwork only works when the legs stop bracing.

stages.title: First footwork
stages.description: Small, fast, on the spot. These six live in almost every house combo you will ever learn.

steps.title: Toe twist
steps.description: Pivot on the balls of both feet, torso quiet. The foundation of the whole twist family.

steps.title: Heel twist
steps.description: Same idea, weight back on the heels. Feels wrong at first — that is the point, it opens a different set of exits.

steps.title: Snap kick
steps.description: Heel lifts, then snaps back down. Your first accent — a step that makes a sound.

steps.title: Knock
steps.description: A knee-in knock counted out loud. Drill it slowly; the count is what stops it drifting off the beat.

steps.title: Ball change
steps.description: Weight from one foot to the other and back. The connector that gets you out of any step and into the next.

steps.title: Farmer
steps.description: High knee lifts with a swinging arm. The knee-up with attitude, and the first step that reads from across the room.

stages.title: Travel
stages.description: Everything so far happens in one square foot. Now cover ground without dropping the bounce.

steps.title: The slide
steps.description: One foot glides while the other holds. The cleanest way to leave the spot you have been drilling on.

steps.title: Forward cross over
steps.description: Step forward, cross the other foot over. Adds direction to the footwork you already have.

steps.title: Shuffle
steps.description: Fast alternating feet with the bounce on top. Where speed starts to matter more than shape.

steps.title: The chug
steps.description: Knees drive down, arms swing through. A down-groove that travels, and a good rest between faster passes.

steps.title: Skate
steps.description: Push off one foot and glide onto the other, like pushing across ice. Reads as effortless travel and hides how much leg it takes.

steps.title: Train
steps.description: The long-distance step: quick alternating pushes that carry you across the whole floor in a straight line.

stages.title: Turns, spirals and drops
stages.description: Add the vertical axis. Everything here needs the pulse from stage one or it turns into gymnastics.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.description: A circular sweep of the upper body over quiet feet. Your first move that changes which way you are facing.

steps.title: Spiral
steps.description: Corkscrew toward the floor through a stepped rotation and come back up without stopping. Slow it down until the descent is one continuous line.

steps.title: Lofting
steps.description: The airy half of house — skips, glides and suspended steps that float above the beat instead of driving into it.

steps.title: Twist into a freeze
steps.description: Twist the torso and cut it dead on a held pose. Learning to stop is as much of a skill as learning to move.

steps.title: Helicopter
steps.description: One leg sweeps under the body while the hands take the weight. The floor move most house dancers reach for first — treat it as advanced and warm up properly.

stages.title: Variations
stages.description: The same twists with something extra on top. This is the stage that builds real coordination — do not skip it to get to the combos.

steps.title: Toe twist into a knee up
steps.description: Stage-two toe twist with a knee lift laid over it.

steps.title: Toe twist into a leg curl
steps.description: Same base, heel curls up behind you. Watch that the bounce survives the curl.

steps.title: Heel twist into bedrock
steps.description: Heel twist that rocks side to side. Adds a lateral shift to a step that was going nowhere.

steps.title: Twist separate
steps.description: Torso twists one way, feet step apart the other. Two directions at once.

steps.title: Knock into a hurdle
steps.description: The knock with a jump over an imaginary hurdle. Land on the balls of the feet and straight back into the bounce.

steps.title: Heel twist into jacking in the box
steps.description: Fast heel twists under a jacking torso wave. The hardest coordination test on this path.

steps.title: Toe twist into charleston
steps.description: Toe twist that borrows the charleston kick. House takes from everywhere — this is the clearest example.

stages.title: Put it together
stages.description: Steps are vocabulary. These are sentences.

steps.title: Foundational combo class
steps.description: A full hour building the stage-two and stage-three steps into one combo. Do it once through slowly, then at tempo.

steps.title: Jacking and skating combo
steps.description: Shorter choreo that alternates torso grooves with quick travelling footwork.

steps.title: Freestyle a track end to end
steps.description: No counts, no mirror. Put on one house track and keep the jack running for the whole thing — swap steps whenever you feel the music change. This is the actual goal of the path.
